prompt.en: Ink marks are drawn 1 mm apart along a young root, starting at the tip. Two days later, which marks have moved apart, and which have not? Explain why, using what you know about the cells at a root tip.

label.en: Only the marks near the tip move apart

level1.en: Which part of the root grows longer: the part near the tip or the older part near the base?

clue.en: A root gets longer only in a short region near its tip.

level2Template.en: Only the marks near the ___ move apart, and the marks further back keep their gaps.

label.en: New cells at the tip, cells behind it grow longer

level1.en: What do the cells at the tip do, and what happens to the new cells just behind it?

clue.en: The apical meristem at the tip makes new cells, and these new cells then grow longer.

level2Template.en: The cells at the tip divide to make new cells, and the new cells just behind the tip grow ___.

accepted: longer and push the tip down

text.en: Only the marks near the tip move apart. The marks further back keep the same gaps.
The apical meristem at the tip makes new cells, and the new cells just behind the tip grow longer.
